advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Thread repo_root through config.resolve_model (add a repo_root param, pass req/self._repo_root from runs.py) so step-level model-class resolution reads the run-repo's class table, matching the three ladder call sites.
evidence: config.py:369: `return resolve_model_string(step or workflow or cfg.model)` — no repo_root argument

The three ladder sites all pass it: production_batch_runner.py:99 `resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0], req.repo_root)`; code_review/batch_runner.py:61 `resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0], req.repo_root)`; workflow/runners.py:126 `resolve_model_string(req.model_ladder[0], req.repo_root)`

runs.py:151 `cfg = self._config or LLMConfig.from_env(repo_root=self._repo_root)` shows repo_root IS available and IS threaded for config, but runs.py:154 `model=resolve_model(cfg, step=..., workflow=...)` omits it
load_class_slots(repo_root=None) -> _read_llm_file_table(None) -> read_reserved_section(..., None) -> _discover_project_config(None) discovers config from CWD (config.py:412-423, config.py:595)
advisory.finding: config.resolve_model resolves model-class names against CWD, not the run's repo_root, unlike the three batch-runner call sites which deliberately thread req.repo_root. resolve_model_string is invoked with the default repo_root=None, so load_class_slots -> _read_llm_file_table -> _discover_project_config(None) reads the [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] project table from the current working directory. Its caller RunnerAgentStep.run has self._repo_root available (it passes it to LLMConfig.from_env) but does not forward it, and resolve_model exposes no repo_root parameter. For a workflow run whose repo_root differs from CWD, a per-step `model: standard` resolves against the wrong project's class table (or none), splitting behaviour from the ladder path this change was written to unify.
scenarios: A workflow agent step declares `model: standard` and the process CWD is not the run's repo_root (e.g. a run driven against a scratch/worktree repo): the class table is read from the wrong project, so the step either resolves to the wrong provider target or falls back to the built-in default instead of the run-repo's [tool.rebar.llm.model_classes] table.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add `repo_root: str | None = None` to resolve_model and pass it into resolve_model_string; update RunnerAgentStep.run to call resolve_model(cfg, step=..., workflow=..., repo_root=self._repo_root).

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add tests exercising `_rung_target`'s degrade paths: (a) monkeypatch `resolve_model_string` to raise and assert `models_at_or_above` still returns the bare ladder ids; (b) a ladder rung with no family match returns the bare name.
evidence: sizing.py:344-352: `try: ... resolved = resolve_model_string(class_name) ... except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — best-effort: an unresolvable class must not break escalation\n        return bare`
sizing.py:341-343: `class_name = next((cls for family, cls in _RUNG_CLASSES if family in bare), None)\n    if class_name is None:\n        return bare`

search_files for `_rung_target` across tests/ returns no matches — no test references the function or injects a resolution failure; the only `models_at_or_above` tests use well-formed class tables (bedrock_classes / no_classes) so resolution always succeeds and every ladder rung matches a family.

ABSENCE: no test monkeypatches `resolve_model_string` (or `load_class_slots`) to raise, and no test feeds `models_at_or_above` a ladder rung outside the haiku/sonnet/opus families, so both fallback-to-bare branches are unverified.
advisory.finding: The documented recovery/degrade contract in `sizing._rung_target` is untested: neither the `except Exception -> return bare` branch nor the `class_name is None -> return bare` (no family match) branch is exercised. The commit message calls this a safety guarantee ('escalation is a recovery path and must never become a new failure mode'), yet a regression that let a resolution failure propagate — or mis-handled a rung whose name matches none of haiku/sonnet/opus — would pass the whole suite.
advisory.suggested_fix: Add a test that sets a valid bedrock table but monkeypatches `rebar.llm.model_classes.resolve_model_string` to raise, asserting `sizing.models_at_or_above(_TODAY_STANDARD) == [_TODAY_STANDARD, _TODAY_FRONTIER]` (bare fallback holds); and a test proving a non-haiku/sonnet/opus rung round-trips as its bare name.
